Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.securitycenter

Class SecurityScore

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.securitycenter.SecurityScore
public final class SecurityScore extends Object
The pure, weighted security checklist behind the Overview grade. Given a SecuritySnapshot it scores six defense-in-depth items - SELinux enforcing, the firewall running, an antivirus scanner installed, its definitions known, private (Tor) mode on, and a VPN tunnel up with its kill switch armed - into a 0-100 total and an A-F letter SecurityScore.Grade, plus one SecurityScore.Item per check so the UI can show exactly what passed and what did not.

Nothing here reads the host, spawns a process or touches Swing: the panel probes into a snapshot and hands it to compute(org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.securitycenter.SecuritySnapshot), so the whole scoring contract is unit-testable headless. The two anonymity items (tor, VPN) are deliberately weighted so a host that is fully patched but simply does not run a tunnel still grades well (a B), while a host with everything - including an active, kill-switch-armed tunnel - reaches an A.

    • compute

      public static SecurityScore.Result compute(SecuritySnapshot snapshot)
      Scores a posture snapshot. A null snapshot is treated as the all-unknown SecuritySnapshot.unknown(), which scores zero (an unprobed host is never assumed safe).
      Parameters:
      snapshot - the posture to score
      Returns:
      the weighted result, never null
